title: LoongSage: A Production-Grade, High-Efficiency Agentic RL Framework for Frontier LLMs with Validated Recipes
data_curation: Not a focus of this paper. As a framework report it uses existing task sources for its four validation runs: R2E-Gym tasks for the DeepSeek-V4-Flash SWE run and the Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B black-box OpenCode run, DAPO-Math-17k for the DeepSeek-V4-Flash DAPO run, and a BrowseComp-Plus + DAPO-Math-17k mix for multi-teacher distillation. Its data plane supports per-source agents, rewards and sampling parameters, post-generation admission filtering with configurable per-source over-sampling to refill rejected slots, and keeps the global data-mixture proportions invariant across ranks and mini-batches.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. The framework is designed for composing post-training stages (SFT, then RL, then on-policy distillation) on shared infrastructure, but reports four independent single runs rather than a staged pipeline. In multi-teacher on-policy distillation, each data source binds its own teacher, so the data-mixing ratio directly sets each teacher's relative gradient contribution instead of hand-tuned loss weights; distillation can run alone or combined with GRPO/GSPO. SFT, PPO and LoRA are listed as roadmap items.
method: LoongSage is a ~14K-line, fully asynchronous agentic RL framework on Megatron-Core/Megatron-Bridge and SGLang with zero-fork dependencies, a single controller process and GPU components as Ray actors. AgentFlow integrates white-box and black-box agents (OpenCode; Codex and Claude Code adapters in progress) through an OpenAI Chat Completions router with Token-In-Token-Out storage, so trained tokens match sampled tokens; black-box trajectories are stored as segment trees (root/compact/subagent), with only mainline segments trainable. Async mode uses three sliding-window policies (no-window, window-gated with staleness <=S steps, windowed-fifo collecting only within one batch of the oldest in-flight group, the default) with window W=B(1+S). TransferMesh streams packed named-tensor buckets via CUDA IPC (colocated) or NCCL broadcast. A Teacher Manager offloads inactive teachers to CPU and rebuilds full-vocabulary teacher logits per micro-batch from hidden states. Consistency: MoE Rollout Routing Replay (R3), FP32 LM head, THD packing with context parallelism, plus TIS/MIS, M2PO and OPSM corrections. Ten decorator registries expose agents, rewards, losses and scheduling.
eval_metrics: No downstream benchmark scores are reported; validation tracks training entropy, rollout reward mean, K3 train-inference KL, and step time over four full runs plus an async throughput ablation. SWE (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 8 H20 nodes): reward climbs to 0.75-0.80, KL bounded at ~1e-4, steps 4000-5500 s. DAPO (DeepSeek-V4-Flash): reward 0.45 to ~0.80, K3 KL peaks at 5.3e-4 and settles near 4.5e-4, step time 900 to 550 s. OpenCode (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B): reward 0.35 to 0.50, KL ~4e-4. MOPD (Qwen3-30B-A3B, one H20 node): student-teacher entropy gap closes almost immediately, step time 1100 to 700 s, full-vocabulary distillation adds only 17 GB peak memory over DAPO.
key_results: On Qwen3-30B-A3B GRPO (16 H20 GPUs, B=64 x 8, 20K-token responses), fully asynchronous windowed-fifo with S=2 cuts average step time from 580.79 s (colocated) to 428.76 s, a 1.35x speedup (1.40x steady-state), and windowed-fifo gets 4-6% more throughput than no-window with a buffer less than half as deep. Across the four production runs, rewards rise steadily while the train-inference gap stays at the 1e-4 scale.
evolution_note: LoongSage follows slime's minimalist Megatron+SGLang pairing, verl's extensible controller design, AReaL/Forge-style fully asynchronous rollouts and Agent-Lightning's agent-trainer disaggregation. It reacts to frameworks built for single-turn RLHF/RLVR by treating TITO trajectory fidelity, bounded staleness, MoE routing replay and precision pinning as core design primitives, and adds memory-multiplexed multi-teacher on-policy distillation. Its operational appendix, which catalogs silent kernel and weight-layout bugs that widened the train-inference gap, argues that agentic RL recipes must include system configurations, not just hyperparameters.
